messages:
alex: Hey — first week question. My CI started failing with 401s this morning when hitting hosted API. I thought hosted keys don't expire. Anyone know if keys rotate automatically?
emily: hey alex — hosted API keys usually don't auto-rotate. Sandbox keys can expire if created via quickstart. Did you check the key in Console > API keys? :mag:
alex: I checked console, the key shows 'last used: 2026-11-05' and 'created: 2026-03-01'. It's active. The CI job prints 401 though. We use the hosted key in GitHub Actions secrets.
mohit: possible the secret got trimmed/linebreak in GH. also rate-limit vs 401 — 429 is rate limit. 401 is auth. Can you curl from a devbox to confirm?
alex: ran curl:
```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
```
returned 200 locally
mohit: then GH Actions is probably misconfigured or using an expired sandbox key env var. Check repo secrets name and runner env.
emily: for CI we recommend service account keys pinned to org project, not personal hosted tokens. Also consider using the sandbox key for dev/devnet usage; hosted keys are for prod traffic.
oncall-bot: Reminder: rotate prod keys only during low traffic windows. See playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/key-rotation
maria: I'll open a quick infra ticket to check GitHub secrets and runner logs — @ops-team can you take a look? :+1:
ops-team: digging in now, saw an update to GHA secrets 12:02 UTC — looks like someone renamed SECRET_NAME to REDWOOD_TOKEN_OLD. Rolling fix.
alex: thanks all! pinned the correct secret name, CI green now. Any docs on recommended key types for CI vs dev?
emily: yep — https://docs.redwood.ai/dev-keys. TL;DR: CI -> org service token with minimal scopes; local dev -> sandbox key; production -> hosted with quotas. Ping devex if you want a template.
alex: awesome, appreciate it :heart:
